title: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves

keywords: ali baba and the forty thieves
full_text:
In a bustling town of Persia lived two brothers: Kasim, who married a wealthy heiress and operated a grand shop, and Ali Baba, a humble woodcutter who earned a frugal livelihood gathering fuel in the forest with three donkeys.

One day deep in the woods, Ali Baba heard the thundering gallop of horsemen. Fearing bandits, he tied his donkeys in a thicket and climbed a tall tree leafy enough to conceal him. Forty fierce brigands drew rein before a towering rock face. Their captain dismounted, faced the stone wall, and proclaimed with a ringing voice:
'Open, Sesame!'

A hidden door swung open in the solid rock. The thieves carried heavy saddlebags inside, emerged empty-handed, and the captain commanded:
'Shut, Sesame!' The stone door sealed seamlessly.

When the troop rode away, Ali Baba descended, approached the rock, and repeated: 'Open, Sesame!' To his amazement, the portal opened into a luminous cavern filled with stacks of silk, spices, and mounds of silver and gold coin—the accumulated plunder of generations.

Ali Baba took only what his three donkeys could carry, covered the gold bags with firewood, sealed the cave with 'Shut, Sesame!', and returned home. He revealed the secret to his wife, urging secrecy. Needing to measure the gold coins, his wife borrowed a measuring bowl from Kasim's wealthy wife. Suspicious, Kasim's wife smeared beeswax at the bottom of the vessel. When returned, a gold dinar stuck to the wax!

Kasim confronted his brother, demanding the secret of the hoard under threat of denunciation. Gentle Ali Baba generously shared the secret words and the cave's location.

Greedy Kasim rushed to the cave with ten mules and iron chests. Entering with 'Open, Sesame!', he became intoxicated by the mountain of jewels. But when he turned to leave, his mind, blinded by avarice, forgot the magic word!
'Open, Barley!' he shouted. 'Open, Wheat!'
The rock remained unyielding. Trapped, Kasim trembled until the forty thieves returned. Finding him inside, they slew him without mercy.

When Kasim did not return, Ali Baba searched the cavern, discovered his brother's remains, and brought them home with heavy sorrow.

Now in Ali Baba's household lived Morgiana, an enslaved maiden of extraordinary intelligence, agility, and courage. To preserve the secret and grant Kasim an honorable burial without suspicion, Morgiana devised a clever plan: she engaged Baba Mustafa, an elderly blind cobbler, blindfolded him, and led him through winding lanes to Kasim's house, where he stitched the remains together so a traditional shroud could be fitted.

The captain of the thieves soon discovered that the body had been removed. Realizing someone else possessed the secret, he sent a scout to town. The scout met Baba Mustafa, who boasted that he had sewn together a corpse in a mysterious house. Bribing the cobbler to retrace his steps blindfolded, the scout located Ali Baba's house and marked the door with white chalk.

Alert Morgiana noticed the white chalk mark. Guessing danger, she marked every house in the neighborhood with identical chalk, confounding the bandits. A second spy marked the door with red chalk, but Morgiana again foiled the plot by marking all neighboring doors in red.

Enraged by his scouts' failure, the captain surveyed the house himself, memorizing its shape. He disguised himself as an oil merchant traveling with nineteen mules bearing thirty-eight large leather jars: one filled with olive oil, and thirty-seven concealing his armed men!

Arriving at Ali Baba's gate at dusk, the disguised captain requested hospitality, which hospitable Ali Baba gladly granted, having the jars stacked in the courtyard.

During the night, Morgiana's oil lamp went out. Seeking a cup of oil from the courtyard jars, she approached one and heard a whisper from within:
'Is it time, Captain?'
Morgiana, never losing her presence of mind, replied in a deep whisper: 'Not yet, but soon.'

Discovering thirty-seven armed killers hidden inside the jars, Morgiana acted decisively. She heated a massive caldron of boiling oil and poured enough into each occupied vessel to instantly incapacitate the assassins, saving her master's entire family.

When the captain gave the signal to strike and received no answer, he found his gang destroyed and fled into the night.

Months later, the captain returned disguised as a merchant of fine silks named Kogias Hassan, befriending Ali Baba's son and becoming a guest at dinner. But sharp-eyed Morgiana recognized his face beneath the false beard and noticed a concealed dagger in his belt.

During the banquet, Morgiana dressed as a traditional dancer, performing an intricate, swirling dance with a silver dagger to the sound of the tambourine. Whirling closer to the false guest, she plunged the dagger into his black heart before he could draw his weapon!

Ali Baba cried out in horror, but Morgiana revealed the hidden dagger and unmasked the bandit captain.
Weeping with gratitude, Ali Baba embraced Morgiana, gave her her freedom, married her to his beloved son, and endowed her with half the mountain treasure. For generations, the family used the secret cave with moderation, using the gold to feed orphans, heal the sick, and bless the poor of Persia.
moral: Greed and arrogance dig an early grave, but loyalty, sharp wit, and discretion overcome the deadliest perils.
